title: PowerTOST's p(BE-ABEL) is the mixed decision, and power.scABEL is empirically tuned
raised_by: source inspection during PR #60, before any comparison fixture was written
status_note: No classification, because nothing was resolved: the wrong comparison was never written, so there was no discrepancy to explain. PREEMPTED is what the VAL-FDA-HVD-001 rule produces when it works.
why_it_was_looked_for: VAL-FDA-HVD-001 cost a full investigation to discover that p(BE-sABEc) is the mixed decision rather than the scaled criterion. Its recorded conclusion was that verifying a reported quantity's actual meaning must become a standard step before writing any oracle comparison. This is that step, performed first, which is why no incorrect EMA comparison was ever run.

finding_1_naming.claim: p(BE-ABEL) is the mixed decision - ABEL above the switch, conventional ABE below - not the ABEL criterion alone.
finding_1_naming.directly_comparable_anyway: p(BE-pe), the point-estimate constraint, is evaluated over all simulations unconditionally - as in the FDA family.

finding_2_empirical_adaptations.claim: power.scABEL for EMA routes to power.scABEL1, which is a tuned approximation rather than a faithful implementation of the EMA rule.
finding_2_empirical_adaptations.routing: reg_const("EMA") leaves est_method = "ANOVA"; R/power_scABEL.R line 17 routes on that to power.scABEL1.
finding_2_empirical_adaptations.header_comment: power via key statistic sims with empirical adaptions to obtain better agreement to sims based on subject data

adaptations.source: s2wT is empirical because dfTT is not defined and artificially set to equal dfRR
'mean' of both attempts V1.1-02/V1.1-03 in case of 2x2x4
adaptations.what: mses <- (mses_ABE + (s2wTs + s2wRs)/2)/2 - the average of two different estimators

adaptations.source: #--- conventional ABE for low CV (0.2 is purely empiric)
adaptations.what: a different mean square is used for the ABE branch when CVwR <= 20%

finding_2_empirical_adaptations.consequence: None of this is in the EMA guideline. Comparing be-stats against power.scABEL would compare a faithful implementation against a deliberately inexact one and report the difference as a finding.

oracles_used_instead.establishes: the widened limits exactly, with no simulation and no Monte Carlo tolerance

oracles_used_instead.oracle: EMA/618604/2008 Rev. 13 Data set I and II
oracles_used_instead.establishes: Method A point estimate, 90% CI and CVwR against the regulator's own published numbers
available and adaptation-free (it fits real lm() models), but reports the same mixed p(BE-ABEL)

scabel_notes: The switch MATCHES the regulator: widening applies for CV > 0.3 (with a 1e-10 tolerance), which is EMA's strict >30%. Unlike VAL-FDA-HVD-002, PowerTOST and the regulator agree here.

The lower limit is computed as 1/upper rather than exp(-k*sWR) - equal in exact arithmetic, possibly a last-ULP difference in floating point. EMA states the pair symmetrically as exp[+/- k.sWR], which is what be-stats computes.
The cap is computed from CVcap rather than taken from the guideline's stated pair. That is VAL-EMA-ABEL-002.
